keyframe_review.note: Valid for 911-925 with the correction. Cliopatria's 416,709 km2 covers 98 percent of Hunan, 49 percent of Guangxi, 23 percent of Guizhou, 18 percent of Hubei, 8 percent of Jiangxi and 6 percent of Guangdong; the Ma Chu page says the kingdom 'ruled over present-day Hunan and northeastern Guangxi' and the Ma Yin page repeats 'roughly modern Hunan and northeastern Guangxi'. The Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi and Guangdong fringes and the central Guangxi cells have no page, and Ji (lost 909), Yuan (lost 914) and Rong and Gao (lost 911) left the realm. The corrected shape is about 296,000 km2, 0.71 of Cliopatria; the pages give no infobox area.

wars.name: Chu-Hongnong (Yang Wu) and Jingnan wars
wars.outcome: No lasting change on the opened page: Yue fell to Huainan in 906 and was regained in 907; Ji was lost in 909 and Yuan in 914; in 919 'Chu forces attacked Jingnan, and Gao Jixing sought aid from Wu'; Wu's Li Jian captured Chu's Fu Prefecture and Chu withdrew.

notes: Cliopatria's Southern Chu row (911-959, three near-identical shapes of about 416,700 km2) overshoots the pages twice. In space it adds Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi and Guangdong fringes and central Guangxi that no page names; keyframes 908 to 947 cut it to Hunan, the Guilin country and the Wuzhou country (about 296,000 km2). In time it runs eight years past the end: the Ma Chu page ends the kingdom in 951 and the Southern Tang page has the Southern Tang in Tanzhou until 1 December 952; the 952-963 land is the Wuping Jiedushi (Liu Yan 952-955, Wang Kui, then Zhou Xingfeng 956-962, Song 963), which needs its own dossier (suggested slug wuping-circuit, group ea-04); the opened pages (Ma Chu, Southern Tang, Pan Shusi) are too thin on it to write one here. Page disagreement on the founding: the Ma Chu page's infobox gives 907 ('Became the State') and 927 ('establishment of the Kingdom'), the Five Dynasties page also gives 927 in one section; this dossier starts on 907, when the Later Liang created Ma Yin Prince of Chu, and takes 927 as the Later Tang's confirmation of the title ('King of Chu'). Left out of the ledger because the pages cannot place or date them: the loss of Ji (Jiangxi) in 909, of Rong and Gao in 911 ('Ningyuan territory') and of Yuan in 914, and the 919 loss of Fu Prefecture; none is inside the corrected outline. Nominal ties are not drawn as vassal tints: tea tribute to the Later Liang, tribute to the Later Tang in 923 and its 927 investiture, and the Southern Tang's confirmation of the Prince of Chu in 927 (Five Dynasties page); the Southern Tang page does say 'Ma Xi'e became a vassal of the Southern Tang in 951', a relation the Southern Tang dossier owns. Who took the Guilin and Wuzhou country after 951 is on no opened page. Pages that did not help: Zhou Xingfeng redirects to the Pan Shusi biography.
